newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia working days lost to strikes up in May.
newsitem.headline: Australia working days lost to strikes up in May.

text.p: The number of working days lost in Australia through industrial disputes increased to 65,200 in May, up from 36,300 a month earlier, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
The number of disputes rose to 43 in May from 40 in April and the number of employees involved climbed to 55,700 from 30,700.
Education, health and community services, which lost 21,900 working days in the month, was the worst-hit sector.
Queensland was the worst-hit state, losing 32,700 days in the month.
The bureau said 731,900 working days were lost in the year to May, an increase of 26,900 days or four percent over the preceding 12 months.

The construction industry lost the most number of days through the year, with 251,500, ahead of coal mining with 144,000, and education, health and community services with 131,700. -- Canberra Bureau 61-6 273-2730
